requirements.note: 4-across square centre-cropped grid with ~2pt gaps, oldest at top, opens scrolled to the newest at the bottom, day headings per day, '1,500 Photos' footer like Photos.

Opens full screen at the photo's own aspect ratio; swipe left goes to the next photo and swipe down closes. A rightward swipe at normal speed (800–1200 pt/s) closes the viewer instead of going to the previous photo; only a fast flick (≥2000 pt/s) pages back.
The heart toolbar button toggles (Favorite/Unfavorite) and a white heart badge appears on the thumbnail in the grid.
Albums tab with large title lists all 8 albums in a 2-column grid with rounded covers, names and counts (summing to 1,500); tapping one pushes a grid with back button, Select and a count footer.

Select → tap to check (blue checkmark), Select All/Cancel, nav title 'N Photos Selected'; Favorite applies to all; Delete shows a system confirmation popover 'Delete 2 Photos' and removes them, with counts updated.
After relaunch the favorites and deletions were kept (1,498 Photos, hearts still shown, album counts updated).

bugs: Full-screen viewer: a normal-speed swipe right dismisses the viewer back to the grid instead of showing the previous photo; going backwards needs a fast flick.
tells: In select mode at the largest text size, the '1,498 Photos' footer draws underneath and between the heart and trash toolbar buttons and collides with them.
At the largest text size the select-mode title is truncated to '1 Photo Sel…' between the Select All and Cancel buttons.
Entering select mode shifts the grid content down about 49pt as the tab bar hides, so the photo under your finger moves.
Day headings sit 8pt from the edge, tighter than the system's 16–20pt layout margin.
A.scroll: Native-feeling collection view: slow drags and hard flings are smooth with no blank or popping tiles, status-bar tap scrolls to the top, rubber-band past the top works, and scroll position is kept across tab switches and viewer round-trips.

requirements.note: 4-across square centre-cropped grid with thin gaps, oldest at the top, opens at the newest at the bottom; 48pt day headings; large 'Library' title with a '1,500 Photos' subtitle.
Opens on black at the photo's aspect ratio, with the date, 'N of 1,500' and the album name; swiping left and right (even slowly) pages in both directions; swipe down and Close both dismiss.
The heart in the viewer toggles favorite and the grid thumbnail shows a heart badge.
Albums tab ('My Albums' section) lists all 8 albums with covers and counts, plus an extra 'Utilities > Favorites' album; tapping one pushes its grid.

Select shows empty selection circles, a 'N Photos Selected' title and a bottom bar with heart and trash; favoriting applies to all and exits select mode; Delete shows a centred alert 'Delete 2 photos?' and removes them. There is no Select All.
After relaunch the favorites and deletions were kept (1,498 Photos, hearts kept, album counts updated).

bugs: At the largest text size the expanded large title 'Library' overlaps the status bar clock.
At the largest text size the collapsed nav bar shows a small 'Library' with a huge '1,498 Photos' subtitle spilling over the content.
tells: The select-mode bottom bar is a hand-drawn opaque grey strip (not a system toolbar or Liquid Glass) and repeats the 'N Photos Selected' title.
Viewer chrome (close, heart and trash circles) and the select-bar icons scale with Dynamic Type into giant glyphs, unlike system bar buttons.
Album tiles are exposed to accessibility as 'Link' elements, which is web-like; the viewer's favorite is a Switch wrapped in generic containers.
Batch delete uses a centred alert rather than an action sheet or popover anchored to the trash button, as Photos does.
The extra Favorites album uses a huge full-width cover that breaks the 2-column rhythm.
Select mode has no Select All.
B.scroll: Smooth through slow drags and hard flings with no blank tiles or pop-in; status-bar tap scrolls to the top, the large title collapses correctly, and position is kept across tab switches.

why: Both apps meet nearly every requirement and both lists scroll equally well. A is the more convincing iOS app (system toolbars, an anchored delete popover, Select All), but its viewer breaks a core gesture: a normal swipe right closes the photo instead of going to the previous one. B's flaws are mostly cosmetic and mostly appear at the largest text size (a hand-drawn select bar, giant chrome, the title colliding with the status bar), so it is the app I would rather use and ship.
